## 1. Claim and surface (echoed unchanged)

**Claim under test:** "multiply(3,4) currently returns 12, so the test 'multiply(3,4) is 12' in src/multiply.test.js passes."

**Surface:** the fixture as it stands — `src/multiply.js`, `src/multiply.test.js`.

## 2. Falsification attempts and results

| # | Attempt | Command / input | Observed result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read the candidate source before running anything | `cat src/multiply.js` | Body is `return a + b;` with an in-source comment `// BUG: adds instead of multiplying` |
| 2 | Read the test to check it is not vacuous | `cat src/multiply.test.js` | Real assertion: `assert.strictEqual(multiply(3, 4), 12)` under `node:test`; no skip/todo, no empty body |
| 3 | Direct evaluation of the claimed return value | `node -e "…console.log(multiply(3,4))"` | **`7`** (typeof `number`) — not `12` |
| 4 | Execute the exact named test | `node --test src/multiply.test.js` | **FAIL**, exit `1`: `pass 0 / fail 1`, `AssertionError … 7 !== 12`, `actual: 7, expected: 12` |
| 5 | Module-shadowing / resolution check | `ls node_modules`, `grep -rn multiply .` | No `node_modules`; only one `multiply` definition; test resolves `./multiply` to the buggy file. No alternate implementation could be masking the result |
| 6 | Whole-suite adjacent check | `node --test` | Same `multiply` failure reproduces in the full-suite run; the failure is not an artifact of single-file invocation |

The cheap read (attempts 1–2) already exposed the defect, so execution was used only to pin a concrete, quotable counterexample rather than to search for one.

## 3. Analytical result

**refuted.** Both conjuncts of the claim are false, from one root cause: `multiply` adds instead of multiplying. `multiply(3,4)` returns `7`, not `12`; consequently the test named `'multiply(3,4) is 12'` **fails** rather than passes. Confidence: high — the counterexample is deterministic, reproduced by both direct evaluation and the real test runner, with no shadowing path that could change the outcome.
